question.text: Kaveri Credit Opps funds INR 100 crore of mezzanine debt at a 12% cash coupon + 3% PIK + 2% equity warrants (strike at current round). 3-year bullet repayment. At exit, the equity warrants convert and are sold for INR 25 crore additional proceeds. Approximate gross IRR (ignoring fees)?

answer.text: Approximately 21-22% — cash coupon + PIK compounded + warrant equity uplift, reflecting the typical mezzanine IRR range of 18-22%.
35% — higher than venture debt returns cited in Chapter 9.

explanation.text: The Logic: Cash coupon 12% p.a. on 100 cr = 12 cr/yr × 3 = 36 cr. PIK 3% compounds: 100 × (1.03)^3 - 100 = 9.27 cr. Principal repaid 100 cr. Warrant sale 25 cr. Total inflows ≈ 100 + 36 + 9.27 + 25 = 170.27 cr on 100 cr outflow over 3 yr. IRR ≈ (170.27/100)^(1/3) - 1 ≈ 19.4% (simple 3-yr approx, 19-22% with annualised timing). Chapter 9's 18-22% mezz IRR range fits. The Trap: Options A and B ignore the equity-kicker contribution. Option D overshoots — Chapter 9 cites venture debt IRRs up to 25-30%, but a SaaS-IPO mezzanine is typically 18-22%. Cross-Exam Context: XV tests IRR math. XIX-A tests concept only. XXI-B (PM) is listed-only. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always model IRR on a cash-on-cash (not gross-yield) basis in the IC note. A 12% coupon with late bullet repayment and early warrant exercise can produce a 25%+ IRR — LPs care about timing, not just headline yield.
